documented_divergences.scope: The controlled no-join scores agree to 3e-8, so target scaling alone does not explain the joined-score gap. With the join, legacy reuses outer OOF base predictions that were fit using the current fold's validation labels; DAG-ML refits within the outer train and scores its held-out fold. The CV scores therefore describe different fit scopes and need not match. This evidence does not promise numerical convergence of every PLS fit or identify every source of a score difference in other datasets.

documented_divergences.classification: legacy passes each CV validation fold to AutoGluon as tuning_data
documented_divergences.evidence: autogluon_model.py:_train_model; test_dagml_autogluon_model.py; test_dagml_autogluon_native.py against real AutoGluon 1.6.1; direct TabularPredictor two-scope control on the same StratifiedKFold rows
documented_divergences.scope: The DAG-ML host adapter trains AutoGluon on fold-train rows only and lets AutoGluon select its internal holdout. Giving the CV validation labels to the operator would leak the evaluation fold into fitting. On one 100-row binary LightGBM case, public legacy scored 0.919 versus DAG-ML 0.500. A direct AutoGluon 1.6.1 control on those same folds predicted only class 1 with internal holdout (balanced accuracy 0.500 in each fold), but predicted both classes when given the CV validation rows as tuning_data (balanced accuracy 0.941 and 0.897). This explains this case's score gap and does not make legacy validation leakage a target contract.

gaps.classification: operator-specific cross-language codec and executor boundary; generic DAG-ML Raw transport is implemented
gaps.legacy: A single-output fitted sklearn Ridge archive replays through legacy BundleLoader; the current public nirs4all.predict API rejects legacy bundles under the native migration policy. A legacy independent by-source archive can be written but cannot replay (separate documented divergence).
gaps.dagml: PyO3 and CLI both fit Ridge, export a general .n4a with one Python joblib host artifact, and replay it through public nirs4all.predict; PyTorch customizable_decon also has Python-host archive replay tests on both mechanisms. This host archive has no portable Raw package reference. DAG-ML Core, C, WASM, PyO3 and persistent CLI already transport signed Raw bytes with export/hydrate/release; a Methods PLS N4MM codec proves cross-language replay. The generic byte protocol cannot define sklearn or arbitrary Python object inference in C/Rust/WASM.
gaps.evidence: test_python_host_archive_boundary.py (legacy BundleLoader and DAG PyO3/CLI Ridge replay plus host archive shape); test_dagml_torch_models.py:test_builtin_customizable_decon_run_export_replay; test_dagml_cli_full_train.py:test_legacy_by_source_auto_archive_has_no_replayable_model; dag-ml-cli cli_replays_portable_methods_pls_payload_in_fresh_process; dag-ml core/C/WASM/PyO3 Raw package and persistent_process_controller_roundtrips_portable_raw_artifact_frames
gaps.proposed_contract: Keep arbitrary Python estimators as explicit Python-host artifacts. To make a particular operator portable, define a versioned language-neutral codec for its fitted state and matching inference controller in each target language, then prove fresh-process and cross-language replay. Do not label joblib/cloudpickle bytes Raw portable merely because the generic transport accepts bytes.

A ResidualModel used as another ResidualModel's base returns empty outer predictions and is not functional.

gaps.legacy: nirs4all exposes host HPO through its Python pipeline API
gaps.dagml: Rust core, PyO3, C ABI, standalone CLI, WASM and R/MATLAB CLI wrappers expose host HPO scheduling. Python nirs4all has real RandomForest HPO on both PyO3 and CLI, plus Ridge-residual and PyTorch model-local HPO evidence. The CLI R optimizer now drives a real R Ridge operator on the plan FoldSet; Octave optimizer JSONL still uses synthetic Python operator predictions. Node WASM workers and real Chrome module Web Workers now fit host-local scalar ridge on fold-train IDs, and check native per-fold/pooled OOF RMSE, parallel trials, pruning and resume. R local Ridge HPO is qualified for this two-row numerical oracle; Octave/MATLAB local operators remain unqualified. CI requires R/Octave/browser protocol gates and now a real R Ridge operator gate. Local R 4.6 is available through Miniconda; Octave/MATLAB are absent. Broader R operators, full-train REFIT and artifact replay need separate qualification.
